summary: The Dreamer's model-facing instructions are now versioned, hashed, hot-reloading files an operator can edit without a rebuild — and every row the Dreamer writes records which revision produced it.
details: The Dreamer's instructions used to be ~9,500 characters of Python constants compiled into the image: no version, no hash, no reload. They are now Markdown files with frontmatter under nora/dreamer/ — one doctrine (who the Dreamer is on every run: it looks and does not act; a source that does not mention something has not said it is false; «I could not check» is a result to report) plus one objective per adaptor.

nora/dreamer/ is bind-mounted read-only into the container and reloads on mtime, so editing an objective takes effect on the next Dreamer tick with no rebuild and no restart. Verified against a real read-only directory mount, including an editor's atomic save (which replaces the file's inode), with the change picked up by a live store that was never restarted.

Every room-lexeme and room-exchange row now carries the instruction_sha256 of the text that produced it, so two corpora written either side of an instruction edit can be told apart — the question that could not be asked when the Dreamer glossed 'big walk' (a co-op puzzle video game) as a nighttime stroll.
Each Dreamer tick logs instruction_versions={…}, the way a tag start already logs doctrine_versions={…}, so a trace ties to a revision without opening the database.
A malformed or missing instruction file now refuses startup with the filename in the message, rather than becoming a Dreamer that quietly stops writing rows hours after the deploy that broke it.
New optional [dreamer] config section (dir, reload, strict). A config.toml written before it existed keeps loading unchanged.
limitations: The objectives are still one-shot extraction prompts, lifted byte-for-byte from the constants they replace — this change moves where the text lives and changes no word of it. The read/act split, the tool loop and the per-adaptor budget are the Dreamer runtime, which is a later phase.

The Dreamer's doctrine ships as a versioned artifact but no adaptor sends it to a model yet, so it is deliberately not part of the instruction_sha256 a row carries. It joins both the prompt and the digest in the same change, when each adaptor's instructions are re-partitioned.

room_portrait rows carry no instruction_sha256: that synthesizer makes no model call, and stamping a hash of text that did not produce the row would be provenance bound to the wrong thing. Its provenance is the lexeme and exchange rows it was built from, which now carry their own stamps.
